title: Thermodynamic Constraints

html: In biological neural networks, information is metabolically expensive. Action potentials and synaptic transmission consume significant ATP; consequently, the brain is under valid evolutionary pressure to represent the world using the minimum number of active neurons. This physical constraint naturally enforces a sparse coding regime 1, which is a proxy for model complexity. A "good model" in the brain is literally a "cheap model"–one that explains sensory variance with the fewest spikes (lowest description length LL). Thus, the minimization of variational free energy is not merely a statistical goal but a thermodynamic one: by compressing representations, the agent minimizes its metabolic load.
